data.text: React Router is the standard routing library for React. It keeps UI in sync with the URL using dynamic segments, loaders, and actions.

data.title: React Router v6 setup

data.text: A path segment written as `:name` becomes a dynamic parameter. Inside the matched component, `useParams()` returns those values, which is how you build detail pages such as `/users/:id` without writing a route per user.

data.title: Reading a route parameter

data.text: Nested routes let a parent layout render shared chrome — navigation, sidebar, header — while a child route fills the content area. The parent renders `<Outlet />`, which is replaced by whichever child route matches the URL.

data.title: A shared layout with Outlet

data.text: A `loader` fetches data before the route renders, so the component reads it with `useLoaderData()` instead of showing a loading spinner. If a loader throws, the nearest `errorElement` renders, which gives you a single place to handle a failed request.

data.title: A route loader with an error element
Interview angle: routing is state derived from the URL
data.text: The reason routers exist is that the URL is the source of truth for location: it is shareable, bookmarkable, and drives the back button. When you describe React Router, say that it maps the URL to a component tree rather than storing navigation in component state, and that the data APIs move fetching out of effects and into the route definition. That framing answers why loaders exist.

terms.definition: Maps a path to a component.
Function to fetch data before rendering.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Data routers add loaders and actions.
